title: Switch off the motor without a spark
story: A small 12 V DC motor is held stalled, so its winding (1 mH, 2 ohm) carries 6 A. At t = 1 ms the switch Q1 opens. When open, the switch still leaks like a 10 k ohm resistor. Without help, the winding's current will force a huge negative voltage at node a. Put a part across the winding (from ground to node a) that keeps node a above -5 V when the switch opens, but takes no current while the motor is running.

goals.label: node a never goes below -5 V
the protection part takes less than 1 mA while the motor runs

hints: At the instant the switch opens, the 6 A in the winding must keep flowing. Through which path, and with what voltage?
A diode from ground (anode) to node a (cathode) is reverse-biased while node a is at +12 V, and conducts as soon as node a goes below about -0.7 V.
